name: dnaa-context-condition-landscape
objective:
Background context — answer "why glycerol, why acetate?" in one place. This is a documentation
study, not a research unit; no new mechanism, no parameter changes. It surfaces the existing
v2ecoli media-condition landscape, the multi-fork-replication constraint that drove the
Stage 1 PDF's choice of ABT minimal glycerol, and the reasoning behind using acetate as the
v2ecoli ↔ vEcoli equivalence reference. Everything downstream (Studies 0-8) rests on this
framing.
description:
Sits ahead of Study 0 in the investigation. A reader landing on the chromosome-cycle-calibration
investigation should read THIS first — five minutes here will save twenty minutes of "wait,
why are they running two different conditions?" later.

Three things to take away:

1. **v2ecoli ships with 5 canonical conditions, none of which are ABT glycerol.** The set —
   `with_aa` (τ=25 min), `basal` (τ=44 min), `succinate` (τ=82 min), `no_oxygen` (τ=100 min),
   `acetate` (τ=136 min). All share C=40 min (replication time) + D=20 min (eclipse), giving
   C+D=60 min globally. Any condition with τ < C+D = 60 min has overlapping replication cycles
   (multi-fork) — that's `with_aa` (and arguably `basal` near the boundary).

2. **The Stage 1 PDF chose ABT minimal glycerol (MIX0-845, τ=150 min) deliberately.** From the
   PDF: "Growth condition is ABT minimal glycerol for wildtype MG1655. This is to guarantee
   non-overlapping cell cycle, which avoids synchronization issue." Multi-fork replication
   creates initiation events that overlap in time and chromosome dosage that's a function of
   where in the cycle each fork sits — both bury the signal the DnaA / replication-initiation
   arc is trying to study. Stage 1 also prescribes C=70 + D=30 (C+D=100 min), pushing the
   multi-fork threshold up too.

3. **Acetate (τ=136) is the closest analog to glycerol in v2ecoli's existing set.** Both have
   1 oriC + 0 active forks at t=0 (non-multi-fork). Both are slow enough that C+D fits within
   τ. Critically — acetate has an established vEcoli implementation on the same kb_default
   simData, so we can run a side-by-side v2ecoli ↔ vEcoli match to verify the v2ecoli refactor
   is faithful. Glycerol doesn't have that reference (it's a NEW condition we added). Acetate
   is therefore the v2ecoli refactor's validation point; glycerol is the Stage 1 deliverable.

The embedded HTML below carries the full per-condition observable table (τ observed,
initial dry mass, mass-fold-change, oriC counts, fork counts, multi-fork yes/no) plus an
animation of the 5 baseline simulations side-by-side. Use it to compare the conditions visually.

purpose.question:
What media conditions exist in v2ecoli, why does ABT minimal glycerol matter for the
DnaA arc, and what role does acetate play in our validation pipeline?
purpose.mechanism:
Documentation-only. No code change, no simulation runs new to this study — the comparison
table embedded below comes from 5 baseline simulations already in the worktree's `out/`
directory and the cross-condition animation already rendered in `docs/`.
purpose.expected_outcome:
A reader who lands on the investigation, opens this study first, and reads the description
+ glances at the embedded table can answer the three "what / why glycerol / why acetate"
questions without needing the upstream chat history.

seeded_from.study: (background — explains the design rationale Study 0 builds on)

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition: Documentation surfaced. Nothing to evaluate beyond "is the framing clear?"
pipeline_gate.notes:
This study does NOT gate anything in the strict sense — it's reference material. The
`enables` link to Study 0 is structural (so the DAG renders with this study in front) but
Study 0 doesn't actually wait on this study's tests to pass.

baseline.name: nominal-baseline-only
baseline.notes: Schema-required nominal baseline entry. This context study runs no simulations of its own — all the per-condition observables in the embedded comparison HTML come from earlier baseline runs in this worktree's out/ directory.

key_assumptions: Stage 1 PDF's stated reason for choosing ABT minimal glycerol ("to guarantee non-overlapping cell cycle, which avoids synchronization issue") is the dispositive rationale, not the τ value itself. Any future condition swap (e.g. another slow medium) must preserve the non-overlapping invariant.

Acetate's role as the v2ecoli ↔ vEcoli reference rests on it being the slowest of the established v2ecoli conditions AND having an established vEcoli implementation we can compare against. If vEcoli adds glycerol natively at some point, that reference role can move.

C and D are global scalars in v2ecoli (same across all conditions). The Stage 1 PDF's C=70 / D=30 prescription applies uniformly when the glycerol cache is built — it does NOT mean the other conditions get the same C/D values in production.

findings.statement:
**[Framing established]** Three takeaways now in one place — (1) v2ecoli's 5 canonical
conditions max out at acetate τ=136; none are ABT glycerol. (2) The Stage 1 PDF chose ABT
glycerol τ=150 specifically to avoid multi-fork replication and the synchronization artefacts
that come with it. (3) Acetate is the v2ecoli ↔ vEcoli equivalence reference because it's
the closest non-multi-fork existing condition AND has an established vEcoli implementation
for side-by-side comparison; glycerol is the Stage 1 deliverable.

evidence.note: Documentary finding — no underlying simulation. The artifact is hand-authored from earlier baseline simulations in this worktree's out/ directory.

conclusion_logic.if_primary_tests_pass:
Context surfaced. Reader can answer "why glycerol, why acetate" in under five minutes from
the investigation card.
conclusion_logic.if_primary_tests_fail:
Not applicable — this study has no primary tests. If the framing isn't clear to a fresh
reader, expand the description or add a second embed.
conclusion_logic.biological_validation:
The multi-fork constraint (Td < C+D → overlapping replication cycles) is a textbook E. coli
fact, not v2ecoli-specific. The choice of ABT glycerol for DnaA studies is consistent with
the broader literature (Cooper-Helmstetter, Wold 1994, Boesen 2024) that uses slow
non-overlapping conditions for replication-timing work.
conclusion_logic.block_downstream:
Nothing blocked. This study is reference material; the strict prerequisites for Study 0
are independent of whether this study is read.

embed_visualizations.name: canonical-acetate-vs-stage1
embed_visualizations.description:
Comprehensive cross-condition comparison HTML hand-authored on this branch. The relevant
sections for the conditions-landscape story are (a) the *Per-condition parameter comparison*
table (τ, observed τ, initial dry mass, mass fold-change, oriC counts, fork counts, multi-fork
yes/no across with_aa / basal / succinate / no_oxygen / acetate with Stage 1 glycerol as the
rightmost column), and (b) the theta-replication animation showing chromosome dynamics across
the 5 canonical conditions. The doc also contains later-stage content (Stage 1 override
simulation, Study 1 read-out panels) that's relevant downstream but not the focus here.
